title: RunAsNode off on macOS: the accessibility host and SSH askpass stop running Ember's binary as plain Node
owns: app/sidecar-host/launch.ts and the macOS AX provider launch, app/main/perception/sidecar.ts (host spawn), app/main/remote/askpass-server.ts and app/askpass/**, app/main/main.ts (an askpass no-window mode, shared hunks), scripts/package/fuses.mjs, scripts/package/layout.mjs, scripts/package/mac-bundle.mjs, .github/workflows/ci.yml (the macos and macos-x64 packaged checks), DESIGN.md and sidecar/*/PROTOCOL.md where they describe the launch

items.text:
Review #177. Today the RunAsNode fuse stays on because helpers run Ember's own binary with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, so any program running as the user can start Ember's binary as Node; on macOS, started so that macOS holds Ember responsible for it (by launchd, say), that process acts with Ember's Accessibility and Screen Recording grants. The owner decided to move the helpers off node mode and turn the fuse off.

Scope (the lead's reading of the code): the privilege only exists on macOS (TCC grants follow the responsible app). On macOS exactly two helpers use node mode: the accessibility sidecar host (app/sidecar-host/launch.ts: ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 running dist/app/ax-sidecar.cjs) and SSH's askpass (app/main/remote/askpass-server.ts writes a #!/bin/sh script that runs `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 exec <Ember> askpass.cjs`). On Windows (the commands' job host, which needs a console-capable child process; the AX host; askpass; the WSL launcher) and Linux (the desk helper) node mode grants nothing a user's own program can't already do. So: turn RunAsNode OFF in the macOS build only (fuses.mjs per OS), keep it on for Windows and Linux with the reason written in fuses.mjs and DESIGN.md, and move the two macOS helpers:
(1) The accessibility host on macOS: start it with Electron's utilityProcess.fork (stdio pipes, its env, serviceName 'Ember accessibility'), keeping the JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout contract unchanged; it must still be the process macOS holds Ember responsible for (so its AX and Screen Recording grants are Ember's): the macOS CI's attribution steps check this. Keep Windows' host launch as it is unless the same change is trivially safe there (say which).
(2) SSH askpass on macOS: the decision says askpass runs as Ember itself in a no-window mode: ssh runs the askpass script, which execs Ember's binary normally with a flag (e.g. --ember-askpass) that main.ts handles first thing: no single-instance lock, no windows, no Dock icon (setActivationPolicy('accessory') before anything shows, or the equivalent), talks the existing askpass protocol to the running Ember (the same socket/pipe and nonce askpass.cjs uses), prints the answer, exits with askpass.cjs's exit codes. If that can't avoid a Dock icon or is unreliable, a fallback that needs no node mode is acceptable (say which and why), e.g. a POSIX sh script using /usr/bin/nc -U with base64-encoded fields; never a new native or npm dependency.
(3) Packaging and CI: fuses.mjs gives macOS RunAsNode:false; the macOS packaged checks in ci.yml (jobs macos and macos-x64: today 'plain Node kept' with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 ... -e 'process.exit(0)') must now prove node mode is REFUSED on macOS (the binary starts as the app or exits, never runs the -e script: check a side effect such as a file the script would write) and the rest stays; Windows and Linux checks stay as they are. layout.mjs / mac-bundle.mjs updated if they reference the node-mode host.
(4) Tests: unit tests for the new launch argv/env per OS (no ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE on macOS), the askpass mode's argument handling and protocol client (pure parts), and fuses per OS. You can't run macOS here: list exactly what the next CI run must show (the AX host answering through utilityProcess, the attribution steps green, askpass over SSH on the macOS SSH job in remote.yml, the fuse check).
The shell package's note: Round 1 (a8e1c4d): mac-bundle.mjs signs with --options runtime and --entitlements. ENTITLEMENTS are allow-jit and allow-unsigned-executable-memory (V8), disable-library-validation (an ad hoc signature has no team ID), device.audio-input and automation.apple-events. After signing it reads back the runtime flag and the entitlements, and it fails closed if the flag is missing or if allow-dyld-environment-variables or get-task-allow is present. The fuses.mjs RunAsNode comment now states the TCC caveat. Round 2 (232ecef), for the verifier's CI point: the macOS runner logs say 'System Integrity Protection status: disabled.' (cilogs/ci133, 2 matches). In both packaged checks (macos and macos-x64), the `codesign --display | grep runtime` line stays unconditional. The DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES probe now runs only when `[[ "$(csrutil status 2>&1)" == *"status: enabled"* ]]`. Otherwise the step prints `::notice::SIP is off on this runner: the DYLD_* check can't prove anything here`. I used a [[ ]] string test rather than `csrutil | grep -q`, so GitHub's `bash -eo pipefail` can't turn an early grep exit into a false result. Checked by parsing the YAML, running `bash -n` on both run blocks, and running the SIP block with stub csrutil (on/off) and stub binaries (one honours DYLD, one ignores it). SIP on: the ignoring binary passes and the honouring one fails the step (exit 134). SIP off: the notice prints and the step goes on. So the DYLD behaviour is unproven in CI on the hosted runners: there only the runtime flag is checked. The docs lines the verifier asked for are in forDocs (docs/** belongs to the docs package). Still left, as in round 1: RunAsNode stays on. The AX sidecar host, the Linux desk helper, the commands' job host, SSH askpass and the WSL launcher all run Ember's binary with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE. So on macOS, a program running as the user can start Ember's binary as Node and, when launchd starts it, act with Ember's Accessibility and Screen Recording grants. Proposal: move those helpers to utilityProcess.fork (stdio pipes) or a small separately signed Node helper, then set RunAsNode:false and drop CI's 'node mode kept' checks. That spans the perception, cmdcore/commands, remote and platform packages. Library validation stays off until Ember has a Developer ID team.
